name: Norway
sub: National sorting rules (avfallsforskriften ch. 10a) with shared Sortere.no symbols: food, plastic, paper, glass/metal and residual at home, plus recycling station and pharmacy.

banana.w: Food scraps become biogas and fertiliser; separate food collection is required nationwide.

eggshell.w: Egg shells are food waste and go with other kitchen scraps.

coffee.w: Coffee grounds and paper filters both go in food waste.

bones.w: Bones are accepted in Norwegian food waste along with meat and fish scraps.

shampoo.w: Empty plastic bottles are plastic packaging; a quick squeeze-out is enough, no need to scrub.

polybag.w: Carrier bags and soft plastic film count as plastic packaging.

chips.w: Plastic crisp bags go with plastic packaging; bags mixing paper and plastic go in residual waste.

tube.w: Squeeze it empty and sort the tube as plastic packaging.

carton.w: In Norway drink cartons are sorted with paper and cardboard, not with plastic.

eggtray.w: Sortere.no says paper; some municipalities suggest food waste, where it soaks up moisture.

box.w: Flatten boxes for the paper bin; take large amounts to the recycling station.

pizza.w: Scrape off leftovers; grease stains are fine in paper. Boxes caked in food go in residual.

newspaper.w: Newspapers are recycled into new paper.

jar.w: Empty glass jars go in glass and metal packaging; the metal lid can go too.

wine.w: Wine bottles carry no pant deposit, so they go in glass and metal packaging.

perfume.w: A glass perfume bottle is packaging, so it goes with glass and metal.

tin.w: Empty food tins are metal packaging and are recycled with glass.

window.w: Window glass is not packaging, and insulated panes can be hazardous; take it to the recycling station.

drinkglass.w: Drinking glass has a different make-up from jars; wrap it and put it in residual waste.

mirror.w: Mirrors are not glass packaging; wrap small pieces for residual, take big ones to the station.

tissue.w: Used tissues go in residual; paper that wiped up food spills may go in food waste.

diaper.w: Diapers mix plastic, pulp and waste, so they are burned for energy.

pad.w: Sanitary products go in residual waste.

battery.w: Batteries are hazardous; return them to shops that sell batteries or to the recycling station.

bulb.w: CFL bulbs contain mercury; hand them in where bulbs are sold or at the recycling station.

meds.w: Pharmacies take back leftover medicines free of charge so they are destroyed safely.

paint.w: Paint with leftovers is hazardous waste for the recycling station.

toy.w: A plastic toy is not packaging; small ones go in residual, big ones to the station.
